title: Cross-border analytics replication simulator and soft-fence policy
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background: Console collects per-tenant usage telemetry that is replicated to multiple regions for analytics and dashboards. Customers with residency constraints require guarantees that (a) replicas do not leave approved regions and (b) transient failovers are observable and reversible. Current replication tests exercise end-to-end pipelines but do not model timing/consistency trade-offs nor simulate partial writes and selective quarantine.

Objective: Build a simulation harness and "soft-fence" policy enforcement prototype that lets operators and policy owners explore how replication lag, sampling, and selective quarantine affect visibility, SLA adherence, and costs. The simulator will drive a policy decision engine which can mark data as "soft-fenced" (replicated copies withheld from cross-border sinks until policy checks pass) and produce actionable telemetry.

Proposal:
- Implement a simulator service in the console-backend team that replays real ingestion traces (anonymized) with controllable parameters: per-tenant replication window, sampling rate, failure injection, and lag distribution.
- Attach a policy evaluator that applies residency rules per-tenant: allowed_regions, fallback_regions, quarantine_threshold_ms, and allowed_staleness. Policy decisions are surfaced as events and stored in a policy-audit topic.
- Develop a soft-fence flow: when a policy violation is detected the simulator marks the message and prevents it from being forwarded to cross-border analytics sinks; instead it routes to a quarantined mirror topic for manual review or automated remediation.
- Add dashboards and alerts in the Console: per-tenant soft-fence rate, expected vs observed replication lag, and cost delta for different soft-fence thresholds.

Trade-offs:
- Stronger enforcement reduces cross-border exposure but increases local analytics incompleteness and operator overhead.
- Simulator accuracy depends on trace fidelity; anonymization may remove signals.
- Soft-fence increases storage and potential latency for analytics queries; must balance by tiering policies (audit-only vs enforced).

Rollout plan: prototype -> internal soak with SRE and privacy team -> canary on low-risk tenants -> gated rollout with opt-in for high-sensitivity customers.

Success metrics:
- Simulator able to replay 24h of anonymized trace with configurable lag distribution within 30m setup time.
- Policy evaluator agreement with expected residency violations >= 95% on historical incidents.
- Soft-fence false positive rate < 2% after tuning.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the simulator and policy prototype; integration with the existing replication controller and tenant-metadata service will be separate follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can replay uploaded anonymized trace and produce per-tenant replication events
Policy evaluator emits audit events and marks messages as soft-fenced
Quarantine mirror topic receives soft-fenced messages and is readable by tools for remediation
Console dashboard displays soft-fence rate, replication lag distribution, and cost estimates
Prototype integration tests and a runbook for manual remediation exist
steps: 1) Build trace ingestion and anonymization loader
2) Implement replay engine with pluggable lag/sampling models
3) Implement policy evaluator and policy-audit topic schema
4) Wire soft-fence routing to quarantine mirror and report events
6) Run internal soak and collect telemetry
7) Iterate thresholds and prepare canary runbook
